findings.issue_text: [BUG] Test cleanup registers removal of an IDP with alias "alias" that was never created (the created aliases are "idp-alias-0" through "idp-alias-19"), so cleanup never removes the 20 created providers. getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) either throws at cleanup time or is a silent no-op on a nonexistent resource, leaking 20 identity providers into the shared test realm and breaking subsequent tests/assertions in this class that count IDPs.

[BUG] Second occurrence of the same wrong-alias cleanup: get("alias") instead of get("idp-alias-20") for the provider created with alias "idp-alias-20". The hideOnLogin IDP created in step 1 is never removed by cleanup, polluting the test realm for later tests in OrganizationCacheTest that assert on realm IDP counts (e.g. getByOrganization assertions).

[BUG] The re-add path for a new searchKey calls cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) while the initial-load path uses startupRevision, so the merged query is registered with a counter value rather than the session's startup revision. An entry added with getCurrentCounter instead of the startup revision can be immediately considered stale/invalidated (or never invalidatable) relative to the session's revision window, causing the merged cache entry holding the other organization's searchKey to be dropped or to survive invalidations it should not survive — the per-organization cached result becomes inconsistent with the store.

[ADVISORY] The change to LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate (excluding org-linked non-public brokers) alters the behavior of every caller of getForLogin across all IdentityProviderStorageProvider implementations, not just the new cache. Any existing deployment or test that relied on getForLogin returning org-linked brokers (e.g. custom storage providers, the non-cached JPA implementation used by default when the cache is disabled) sees a changed login-page IDP set shipped inside a caching PR, making regressions in the non-cached path hard to attribute to this diff.

[ADVISORY] When a cache entry exists but the current searchKey is not in it, the code calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) — a local, non-revisioned invalidation — before rebuilding and re-adding the query, unlike every other invalidation in this class which goes through realmCache.registerInvalidation. Other cluster nodes are never informed that the query entry was replaced with one containing additional searchKeys, so a node that reads the entry between the local invalidate and re-add, or that holds a stale view of the searchKey set, returns a miss and rebuilds with its own searchKey only — repeated per-node churn on multi-node deployments whenever more than one organization's login page is exercised.

[BUG] The second cache-population branch calls cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) instead of passing the `loaded` revision read immediately after invalidation, unlike the first branch which uses the loaded revision (startupRevision protocol). The revisioned query is registered under a revision different from the one the delegate read was performed at, so a concurrent invalidation occurring between the read and the addRevisioned is lost — the stale IDP list stays served from cache indefinitely instead of being discarded, showing removed/disabled identity providers on the login page.

[BUG] The new predicate term dereferences idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) without a null guard on getConfig(), for any IdentityProviderModel whose organizationId is set. An org-linked IdentityProviderModel carrying a null config map (e.g., produced by a custom storage provider or a minimally constructed model during import) throws NullPointerException from getLoginPredicate().test(idp) inside registerIDPLoginInvalidation, aborting the create/update/remove operation with a 500 instead of completing it.

[ADVISORY] The 'query exists but this searchKey is not cached' branch (invalidateObject + re-populate + two-arg IdentityProviderListQuery constructor + addRevisioned) is a distinct new code path with no test in the diff — testCacheIDPForLogin only ever exercises a fresh (null-query) cache per mode. A regression in the merge-branch (wrong constructor argument, wrong revision, or searchKey-mapping bug) would only surface when a second organization's ORG_ONLY/ALL search hits a warm cache, i.e., in production multi-org realms where a stale or corrupted list would be served to org members on the login page.

[ADVISORY] Invalidation coverage depends entirely on IDP mutations flowing through create/update/remove of this provider; the diff has no invalidation (and no verification) for organization linkage changes made through OrganizationProvider's own paths (org.identityProviders().remove, or addIdentityProvider on an already-BROKER_PUBLIC idp with no config change), which is exactly the mutation the update-path javadoc says must invalidate. Step 4 of the test only proves invalidation for the BROKER_PUBLIC config change; if OrganizationProvider links/unlinks an IDP without a corresponding identityProviders().update call, the login caches keep the old membership and users see (or miss) IDPs on the org login page until some unrelated invalidation fires.

[ADVISORY] The BROKER_PUBLIC filter is added to the shared SPI-level getLoginPredicate(), silently changing the semantics of getForLogin for every storage provider implementation (JPA/map-storage) — not just the new cache — while the diff's only test asserts cache entry sizes, not the rendered login-page provider set against the non-cached baseline. Deployments relying on the previous predicate behavior (org-linked non-public IDPs appearing in some getForLogin callers) get a silent behavior change with no test pinning the new contract, so a future revert or divergence between the predicate and the delegate's own org filtering goes unnoticed.

[BUG] The change to getLoginPredicate() silently alters the query semantics of every IdentityProviderStorageProvider implementation (JPA, in-memory, map storage), not just the new cache — org-linked IDPs without BROKER_PUBLIC are now excluded everywhere. This is implementation work not traceable to the stated 'add caching' intent: any existing caller or storage relying on the previous predicate (e.g. org-aware login pages that expected org-linked non-public brokers to appear under FetchMode.ALL/ORG_ONLY) sees changed results even with the cache disabled; the behavior change is hidden inside a caching PR and unreviewable as a semantic change.

[BUG] getForLogin returns organization-aware wrapped models on the cache-miss/invalid path but raw (unwrapped) models on the cache-hit path, breaking the method's contract consistency. Callers that depend on the wrapped OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel behavior (the very behavior the OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean re-check of isEnabled in this diff compensates for) get different objects depending on whether the query was served from cache; the added `idp.isEnabled()` filter in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean line 75/80 is a symptom patch that masks the cache-hit path serving stale/unwrapped state rather than fixing the invariant that both paths return identical models.

[BUG] The test registers cleanup against the wrong alias: `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` uses literal "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so none of the 20 created IDPs are ever removed. get("alias") returns null for a nonexistent provider, so the cleanup lambda throws when invoked (or silently leaks 20 providers into the realm for subsequent tests), making the test's isolation broken and its teardown dependent on a null lookup.

[ADVISORY] The cached-IDP-miss branch (idp == null after registerInvalidation) falls back to the delegate but does so only for this request while the invalidated key was already re-added by another concurrent miss path, and the miss itself indicates cache/invalidation skew that the diff only partially repairs. Maintainers of the login cache get an inconsistency: a single missing IDP triggers full cache invalidation plus delegate fallback, but the second addRevisioned path (query != null with unseen searchKey) uses cache.getCurrentCounter() instead of startupRevision used on the first path — a reviewer diffing the two branches cannot tell which revision anchor is correct, and the divergence invites a stale-entry bug on the next edit.

[BUG] registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate skips invalidation when an IDP's BROKER_PUBLIC config flag changes but its org link and login-qualifying status stay the same. The login predicate (getLoginPredicate) includes `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`, so toggling BROKER_PUBLIC on an org-linked IDP changes what getForLogin(REALM_ONLY/ORG_ONLY, null) returns, but the no-invalidate branch (`getLoginPredicate().test(original) && getLoginPredicate().test(updated) && Objects.equals(original.getOrganizationId(), updated.getOrganizationId())`) never compares that config value — admins flipping an org-linked IDP between public and non-public serve a stale login page (stale IDP shown / new IDP missing) from every node holding the cache entry until it is evicted by some other invalidation or expiry.

[BUG] The new clause in getLoginPredicate excludes org-linked, non-BROKER_PUBLIC IDPs from every fetch mode, including org-specific queries where those IDPs are supposed to be listed. getLoginPredicate is the shared filter the delegate storage providers apply across all FetchMode values; adding `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || BROKER_PUBLIC` means an IDP linked to an organization without the public flag is filtered out even for getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL, thatOrgId) — the org's own login page and member login flow silently lose their non-public broker entries, which per the BROKER_PUBLIC contract are meant to be visible only on the org-specific page (the only place they are ever shown). The integration test only creates org-linked IDPs with BROKER_PUBLIC=true (i >= 10 sets it for all of them), so this regression is invisible to the new test.

[BUG] The cleanup registration calls testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias") with the literal alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, and .get returns null for that nonexistent alias, so the `::remove` method reference dereferences null immediately. The very first loop iteration throws NullPointerException inside the test body (the method reference `null::remove` is evaluated on a null Resource at `get("alias")::remove`), failing testCacheIDPForLogin before any caching behavior is exercised and leaving all created IDPs uncleaned for subsequent tests.

[ADVISORY] The second-level branch of getForLogin builds the replacement query with `cache.getCurrentCounter()` while the initial population path uses `startupRevision`, an asymmetry in revision anchoring that makes the merged cache entry's validity depend on which path populated it. A maintainer changing revision semantics (e.g. startupRevision bump on realm import) must know to update two differently-anchored addRevisioned calls in one method; if the existing-query merge path is ever refactored to the startupRevision anchor or vice versa without understanding why they differ, the login cache either never invalidates (permanently stale login page) or never caches (silent perf regression on the hottest page in Keycloak), and no test distinguishes the two anchors because all tests run on a fresh, single-node cache.

[ADVISORY] getForLogin does not apply createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel on the invalid-entry fallback and relies on getById's internal wrapping for cache hits, so two of the three return paths depend on a different wrapping mechanism than the miss path. The isInvalid branch maps results through createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel explicitly, but the cache-hit loop returns whatever session.identityProviders().getById(id) produces; if getById's wrapping contract ever changes (or a caller compares identity of wrapped vs unwrapped models), login-page rendering behaves differently depending on whether the list cache was warm — a defect class that only reproduces intermittently in production after a cache fill and is invisible to tests that always run one path first.

[BUG] The PR's stated objective is 'add caching support for getForLogin', but the diff silently redefines the getForLogin contract by changing the shared LoginFilter predicate in server-spi so that organization-linked IDPs without BROKER_PUBLIC are excluded, which alters results for every implementation and caller of getForLogin — cached and non-cached alike — without that being part of the announced intent. Any caller of getForLogin outside the organization login page (custom authenticators, third-party providers implementing IdentityProviderStorageProvider) now gets a different set of IDPs than before this PR, with no feature flag or documented API-behavior change; an org-linked IDP that previously appeared in login listings disappears from all login flows, not just the newly cached one.

[ADVISORY] The added `idp.isEnabled()` re-filter (justified by the comment 'idp might have been wrapped') shows the caching layer changed what getForLogin returns — raw/cached models instead of organization-aware wrapped models — and the burden of preserving the previous behavior was pushed into one caller. Only OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean was patched; any other existing or future caller of IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin that relied on receiving pre-filtered, organization-wrapped models (e.g., other login templates or extensions) now receives un-wrapped models that may be disabled or lack organization context, and will silently render wrong login options.

[ADVISORY] The cache-miss path in getForLogin wraps results with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, but the cache-hit path (lines 240-248) resolves IDPs via session.identityProviders().getById(id), which returns the plain cached IdentityProviderModel without the organization-aware wrapping. The organization-aware wrapper is what hides an IDP from the login page when its organization is not public or is member-only (the OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean diff's own 're-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped' comment confirms wrapping can flip enabled state). A user hitting the cached path gets the unwrapped model, so an IDP linked to a non-public organization that was cached under a different organizationId/searchKey context can be rendered on the realm's public login page, disclosing the existence of organization-internal identity providers to unauthenticated users.

[ADVISORY] The new predicate in getLoginPredicate dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null check, and the whole login-visibility decision for organization-linked IDPs now depends on a string config flag parsed with Boolean.parseBoolean, which silently treats any malformed value (e.g. 'true ', 'yes', 'True ' with whitespace) as non-public. An administrator who sets BROKER_PUBLIC via config map/CLI with any casing/whitespace other than exact 'true' gets an IDP silently hidden from all login pages — an availability/visibility failure with no warning at write time; and if getConfig() returns null (as it can for programmatically built models that never had setConfig called), the predicate throws NPE and breaks the login page entirely.

[ADVISORY] Login-cache invalidation is triggered only from the IDP create/update/remove paths in this provider; mutations that change which IDPs are login-visible but are performed through the OrganizationProvider (linking/unlinking an IDP to an organization, or disabling the organization itself) do not pass through these methods, so registerIDPLoginInvalidation is never invoked for them. An admin who unlinks an IDP from an organization (or disables the organization) through the organization management endpoints serves stale cached login lists that still expose the old IDP-to-organization mapping on the public login page until some unrelated IDP write invalidates the cache — a stale-authorization-surface window the diff's own test only avoids because it manually calls the IDP update first.

[BUG] The cleanup registration uses the literal alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so every created IDP is leaked into the realm. getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) resolves to a null resource whose remove() is a no-op against a nonexistent alias, so the 20 created IDPs are never cleaned up and pollute subsequent tests in the same realm; the "disabled IDP" test data (e.g. hideOnLogin idp-alias-20 with Broker-20 display name) can break later login-page or IDP-count assertions.

[BUG] The new predicate conjunct dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null guard, throwing NPE for IdentityProviderModel instances whose config map is null. Any caller of getLoginPredicate() (including the new InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.registerIDPLoginInvalidation paths on create/update/remove) that passes a model with null config crashes with NullPointerException instead of evaluating the filter; the test suite only feeds admin-API-created IDPs (which always have a config map), so this is untested.

[ADVISORY] The test asserts only the cache-entry sizes via IdentityProviderListQuery.getIDPs() and never asserts the contents of the Stream returned by getForLogin(), so the consumer-visible behavior is unverified. A regression in the materialization loop (e.g. the createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapping, ordering, or dropping/duplicating IDPs while the cached id-set stays correct) passes this test; the test would have caught neither a wrong wrapping nor a stream that returns models with wrong organizationId. The assertion `assertEquals(5, identityProviderListQuery.getIDPs("").size())` verifies the cache, not the API contract.

[ADVISORY] The 'cache entry exists but this searchKey is not cached' merge branch (cached == null, invalidateObject + re-add with previous query) is never exercised by the test, which only queries each FetchMode with a single organizationId. The merge constructor new IdentityProviderListQuery(loaded, cacheKey, getRealm(), searchKey, cached, query) and the cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)/addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) sequence run in production whenever two organizations are queried under the same FetchMode in the same realm — the most common multi-org deployment — but the test never calls getForLogin twice with different organizationIds for the same mode, so a broken merge (lost previous searchKeys, wrong revision) ships unverified.

[ADVISORY] The stale-IDP fallback branch inside getForLogin (getById returns null → registerInvalidation and delegate) is untested. The test never simulates a cache entry referencing an IDP that no longer exists (deleted through a non-cached path or cross-node); if this branch throws, mis-sizes, or fails to actually invalidate the cache key, no test in the diff fails. A regression here surfaces as a permanent NPE/empty login page for every user of the affected realm until cache expiry.

[ADVISORY] Removing an IDP that IS available for login (the registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) call in remove()) is never tested — the test only removes the disabled idp-alias-1 to verify the cache is retained. The invalid direction of remove() is asserted only negatively: if registerIDPLoginInvalidation were dropped or its predicate inverted, every assertion about remove() in testCacheIDPForLogin still passes (removing a non-login IDP expects the cache to remain), so stale removed IDPs would be served on the login page with no failing test.

[ADVISORY] The new isEnabled() re-filter in searchForIdentityProviders has no test coverage in this diff — the only test file changed (OrganizationCacheTest) exercises storage-level caching, not the login-page bean. The stated reason for the change (wrapped IDPs may have isEnabled cleared by createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel) is never verified: no test asserts that a broker-public organization IDP whose wrapper disables it is excluded from the login-page bean output. A future refactor of the wrapper making the re-check unnecessary, or breaking it, is invisible to the suite.

[ADVISORY] The miss-for-searchKey branch adds the new revisioned query with cache.getCurrentCounter() while the cold-cache branch uses startupRevision, so the newly cached list for a second organizationId is anchored at a later revision than the entry it replaces and its validity is judged against the wrong baseline. A cluster where another node invalidates the login cache between the getCurrentRevision read and the getCurrentCounter write can serve the freshly-cached (already stale) org-specific IDP list indefinitely, so users see a removed/disabled broker on the org login page after the remove()/update() invalidation has already been processed.

[ADVISORY] The login-cache invalidation on update() relies on every code path that changes an IDP's organization link going through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update(), but organization membership can also be mutated through the organization provider's IDP management (addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider on the org side), and any such path that writes the link without an update() call bypasses registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate entirely. When an organization links/unlinks a broker via the org API, the cached getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL) sets keep the pre-link IDP lists: a broker just linked to (and hidden from login in) an org continues to be offered on the org's login page, and a broker just unlinked disappears from login until some other invalidation clears the cache — a stale-data condition with no timeout bounded by this code.

[ADVISORY] The change to the shared getLoginPredicate() silently reclassifies every existing org-linked broker lacking BROKER_PUBLIC=true (config null, so Boolean.parseBoolean(null) is false) as unavailable-for-login across all implementations, not just the new cache. Any existing deployment with organization-linked identity providers that relied on those IDPs appearing via getForLogin(ALL/ORG_ONLY) loses them from the login page at upgrade time with no migration/backfill step setting BROKER_PUBLIC on existing IDP config rows; admins must manually set the flag per broker to restore previous behavior.

This is visible in both loops/steps in the diff. As a result, the newly created IDPs are not removed by cleanup, which can pollute the realm state for subsequent tests relying on IDP counts.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `getForLogin` caching logic, the initial cache population path does `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`, but the “existing entry, new searchKey” path rebuilds the query and does `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. This inconsistency is visible in the diff and could affect revision/invalidation behavior depending on how `addRevisioned` and `startupRevision` are meant to interact, but the diff alone does not define those semantics, so the claim that it will definitely become stale/incorrect cannot be conclusively verified here.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the shared SPI logic in `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` by adding `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))` (server-spi module). This predicate is not cache-specific and will affect any caller using `getLoginPredicate()` (and therefore potentially `getForLogin(...)` behavior) across all `IdentityProviderStorageProvider` implementations, including non-cached paths. Whether the behavior change is desired isn’t verifiable from the diff alone, but the scope/architecture concern (behavior change bundled into a caching-oriented PR and affecting non-cached providers) is concrete and diff-grounded.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `getForLogin(...)` caching path, when an `IdentityProviderListQuery` exists but lacks the current `searchKey`, the code does `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey);` (see the `if (cached == null)` block) before rebuilding and `cache.addRevisioned(...)`. Elsewhere in this class, invalidation is typically done via `realmCache.registerInvalidation(...)`, including in the same new method when an IDP lookup returns null. The diff therefore supports the finding that this path uses a different invalidation mechanism that may not propagate in the same way as `registerInvalidation`, which could lead to per-node rebuild/churn in multi-node setups when different `searchKey`s are exercised.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `getForLogin` method, the first cache-population branch does **not** pass the `loaded` revision to `addRevisioned`; it passes `startupRevision` (`cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`). So the finding’s core comparison (“unlike the first branch which uses the loaded revision”) is incorrect per the diff. While the second branch does call `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`, the diff alone does not establish that this is wrong or that it causes a lost invalidation without knowing `addRevisioned`/revision semantics from outside the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new predicate term dereferences idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) without a null guard on getConfig(), for any IdentityProviderModel whose organizationId is set. An org-linked IdentityProviderModel carrying a null config map (e.g., produced by a custom storage provider or a minimally constructed model during import) throws NullPointerException from getLoginPredicate().test(idp) inside registerIDPLoginInvalidation, aborting the create/update/remove operation with a 500 instead of completing it.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff adds a new term to `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()`:
```java
.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))
```
For any `IdentityProviderModel` with a non-null `organizationId`, this unconditionally dereferences `idp.getConfig()` and then calls `.get(...)`. The predicate only guards `idp` itself via `Objects::nonNull`, not the config map. The new caching code calls `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)` during create/update/remove invalidation (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation*` in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider`), so a null config map would cause an NPE and can abort those operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'query exists but this searchKey is not cached' branch (invalidateObject + re-populate + two-arg IdentityProviderListQuery constructor + addRevisioned) is a distinct new code path with no test in the diff — testCacheIDPForLogin only ever exercises a fresh (null-query) cache per mode. A regression in the merge-branch (wrong constructor argument, wrong revision, or searchKey-mapping bug) would only surface when a second organization's ORG_ONLY/ALL search hits a warm cache, i.e., in production multi-org realms where a stale or corrupted list would be served to org members on the login page.

adjudication.rationale: The new getForLogin(...) caching logic adds a distinct warm-cache path: when an IdentityProviderListQuery already exists for a given cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode) but query.getIDPs(searchKey) returns null, it invalidates and rebuilds the query using the constructor that takes the previous query (new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query)) and uses cache.getCurrentCounter() for addRevisioned. The added testCacheIDPForLogin only calls getForLogin once per FetchMode with a single organizationId (or null), so it only exercises the query == null branch and never hits the 'query exists but searchKey not cached' branch that would occur when a second organization (different searchKey) queries the same mode against a warm cache. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test gap for a nontrivial new code path, not a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Invalidation coverage depends entirely on IDP mutations flowing through create/update/remove of this provider; the diff has no invalidation (and no verification) for organization linkage changes made through OrganizationProvider's own paths (org.identityProviders().remove, or addIdentityProvider on an already-BROKER_PUBLIC idp with no config change), which is exactly the mutation the update-path javadoc says must invalidate. Step 4 of the test only proves invalidation for the BROKER_PUBLIC config change; if OrganizationProvider links/unlinks an IDP without a corresponding identityProviders().update call, the login caches keep the old membership and users see (or miss) IDPs on the org login page until some unrelated invalidation fires.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there is “no invalidation (and no verification) for organization linkage changes” and that step 4 “only proves invalidation for the BROKER_PUBLIC config change”. But the diff explicitly adds a new test `testCacheIDPForLogin()` whose step 4 performs an organization linkage change via `testRealm().organizations().get(orgaId).identityProviders().addIdentityProvider("idp-alias-20")` and then asserts all `cacheKeyForLogin(...)` entries are cleared (i.e., it *does* attempt to verify invalidation on org-link changes). Also, from the diff alone we cannot conclude that OrganizationProvider linkage changes do not flow through `identityProviders().update(...)` (which would be caught by `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` via the orgId comparison); the alleged gap depends on code paths not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The BROKER_PUBLIC filter is added to the shared SPI-level getLoginPredicate(), silently changing the semantics of getForLogin for every storage provider implementation (JPA/map-storage) — not just the new cache — while the diff's only test asserts cache entry sizes, not the rendered login-page provider set against the non-cached baseline. Deployments relying on the previous predicate behavior (org-linked non-public IDPs appearing in some getForLogin callers) get a silent behavior change with no test pinning the new contract, so a future revert or divergence between the predicate and the delegate's own org filtering goes unnoticed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the shared SPI-level `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` by adding `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`, which affects `getForLogin(...)` behavior for all storage provider implementations, not just the new Infinispan cache wrapper. The added test (`testCacheIDPForLogin`) only asserts cache presence/clearing and cached ID counts, and does not pin the broader behavioral contract (e.g., comparing rendered login-page provider sets or verifying non-cached baseline semantics across providers). This is a concrete, diff-grounded scope/contract-change concern rather than a clearly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The change to getLoginPredicate() silently alters the query semantics of every IdentityProviderStorageProvider implementation (JPA, in-memory, map storage), not just the new cache — org-linked IDPs without BROKER_PUBLIC are now excluded everywhere. This is implementation work not traceable to the stated 'add caching' intent: any existing caller or storage relying on the previous predicate (e.g. org-aware login pages that expected org-linked non-public brokers to appear under FetchMode.ALL/ORG_ONLY) sees changed results even with the cache disabled; the behavior change is hidden inside a caching PR and unreviewable as a semantic change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change global query semantics, not just caching: `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` (in `server-spi`) now adds `idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`, which will filter out org-linked IDPs unless `BROKER_PUBLIC` is true for every `getForLogin(...)` implementation that relies on this predicate. That is a cross-cutting behavior change introduced alongside the caching work. However, from the diff alone it's not verifiable that this new behavior is incorrect (it may be intentional), so it’s better treated as a scope/semantic-change concern rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getForLogin returns organization-aware wrapped models on the cache-miss/invalid path but raw (unwrapped) models on the cache-hit path, breaking the method's contract consistency. Callers that depend on the wrapped OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel behavior (the very behavior the OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean re-check of isEnabled in this diff compensates for) get different objects depending on whether the query was served from cache; the added `idp.isEnabled()` filter in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean line 75/80 is a symptom patch that masks the cache-hit path serving stale/unwrapped state rather than fixing the invariant that both paths return identical models.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin(...)`, the cache-miss/invalid path returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, explicitly wrapping models. But on the cache-hit path it reconstructs results via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns `identityProviders.stream()` without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. From the diff alone, this is a verifiable inconsistency in what the method returns depending on cache state, and it aligns with the compensating `idp.isEnabled()` re-check added in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The test registers cleanup against the wrong alias: `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` uses literal "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so none of the 20 created IDPs are ever removed. get("alias") returns null for a nonexistent provider, so the cleanup lambda throws when invoked (or silently leaks 20 providers into the realm for subsequent tests), making the test's isolation broken and its teardown dependent on a null lookup.

[ADVISORY] The cached-IDP-miss branch (idp == null after registerInvalidation) falls back to the delegate but does so only for this request while the invalidated key was already re-added by another concurrent miss path, and the miss itself indicates cache/invalidation skew that the diff only partially repairs. Maintainers of the login cache get an inconsistency: a single missing IDP triggers full cache invalidation plus delegate fallback, but the second addRevisioned path (query != null with unseen searchKey) uses cache.getCurrentCounter() instead of startupRevision used on the first path — a reviewer diffing the two branches cannot tell which revision anchor is correct, and the divergence invites a stale-entry bug on the next edit.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show two different revision anchors used when caching `getForLogin(...)` results: the initial miss path (`query == null`) does `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`, while the “unseen searchKey” path (`cached == null`) invalidates and then does `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. That divergence is real and could plausibly lead to confusing or inconsistent cache invalidation semantics, but the finding’s stronger claims about concurrent re-add/invalidation skew and a concrete stale-entry bug are not verifiable from the diff alone. The `idp == null` branch does register invalidation and falls back to the delegate for that request, but concurrency effects are speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate skips invalidation when an IDP's BROKER_PUBLIC config flag changes but its org link and login-qualifying status stay the same. The login predicate (getLoginPredicate) includes `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`, so toggling BROKER_PUBLIC on an org-linked IDP changes what getForLogin(REALM_ONLY/ORG_ONLY, null) returns, but the no-invalidate branch (`getLoginPredicate().test(original) && getLoginPredicate().test(updated) && Objects.equals(original.getOrganizationId(), updated.getOrganizationId())`) never compares that config value — admins flipping an org-linked IDP between public and non-public serve a stale login page (stale IDP shown / new IDP missing) from every node holding the cache entry until it is evicted by some other invalidation or expiry.

adjudication.rationale: In `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate`, invalidation is skipped only when `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` and `.test(updated)` are both true and the organization link is unchanged. But the diff also changes `getLoginPredicate()` to include `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. For an org-linked IDP (`getOrganizationId() != null`), toggling `BROKER_PUBLIC` from true↔false necessarily flips the predicate result true↔false, so neither no-invalidate branch can match and the method will invalidate the login caches. The finding’s claim that the predicate stays true while `BROKER_PUBLIC` changes for an org-linked IDP is not supported by the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new clause in getLoginPredicate excludes org-linked, non-BROKER_PUBLIC IDPs from every fetch mode, including org-specific queries where those IDPs are supposed to be listed. getLoginPredicate is the shared filter the delegate storage providers apply across all FetchMode values; adding `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || BROKER_PUBLIC` means an IDP linked to an organization without the public flag is filtered out even for getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL, thatOrgId) — the org's own login page and member login flow silently lose their non-public broker entries, which per the BROKER_PUBLIC contract are meant to be visible only on the org-specific page (the only place they are ever shown). The integration test only creates org-linked IDPs with BROKER_PUBLIC=true (i >= 10 sets it for all of them), so this regression is invisible to the new test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to add `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`. This predicate is not parameterized by `FetchMode` or `organizationId`, so any org-linked IDP without `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` will be filtered out universally, including in `getForLogin(FetchMode.ORG_ONLY, orgId)` / `getForLogin(FetchMode.ALL, orgId)` calls. The services code explicitly has a “public enabled IDPs linked to any org” use-case (ORG_ONLY with null org), implying non-public org-linked IDPs exist and should differ in visibility depending on context; the new global predicate removes them from org-specific results as well. The added integration test indeed only marks org-linked IDPs as public (`i >= 10` sets `BROKER_PUBLIC` for all of them), so it would not catch this regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup registration calls testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias") with the literal alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, and .get returns null for that nonexistent alias, so the `::remove` method reference dereferences null immediately. The very first loop iteration throws NullPointerException inside the test body (the method reference `null::remove` is evaluated on a null Resource at `get("alias")::remove`), failing testCacheIDPForLogin before any caching behavior is exercised and leaving all created IDPs uncleaned for subsequent tests.

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, the cleanup registration inside the creation loops uses `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (literal "alias") rather than the actual created aliases like `"idp-alias-" + i` (and similarly after creating `idp-alias-20`). This means the cleanup will target the wrong IDP and will not remove the created IDPs, potentially polluting subsequent tests. The finding’s claim about an immediate NPE is not verifiable from the diff (the admin client `.get(String)` typically returns a proxy resource), but the incorrect alias in cleanup is a concrete defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The second-level branch of getForLogin builds the replacement query with `cache.getCurrentCounter()` while the initial population path uses `startupRevision`, an asymmetry in revision anchoring that makes the merged cache entry's validity depend on which path populated it. A maintainer changing revision semantics (e.g. startupRevision bump on realm import) must know to update two differently-anchored addRevisioned calls in one method; if the existing-query merge path is ever refactored to the startupRevision anchor or vice versa without understanding why they differ, the login cache either never invalidates (permanently stale login page) or never caches (silent perf regression on the hottest page in Keycloak), and no test distinguishes the two anchors because all tests run on a fresh, single-node cache.

adjudication.rationale: In `getForLogin`, the initial cache population path does `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`, but the “existing query present, new searchKey not cached” replacement path does `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())` after `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)`. That asymmetry is directly present in the diff and is a legitimate maintainability/consistency concern: future changes to revision/anchoring semantics would need to update two different anchors in the same method, and the added test (`testCacheIDPForLogin`) exercises only single-node fresh-cache behavior and doesn’t distinguish the two anchoring choices. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove this is currently incorrect behavior (it may be intentional), so it’s not a verifiable bug from the PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getForLogin does not apply createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel on the invalid-entry fallback and relies on getById's internal wrapping for cache hits, so two of the three return paths depend on a different wrapping mechanism than the miss path. The isInvalid branch maps results through createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel explicitly, but the cache-hit loop returns whatever session.identityProviders().getById(id) produces; if getById's wrapping contract ever changes (or a caller compares identity of wrapped vs unwrapped models), login-page rendering behaves differently depending on whether the list cache was warm — a defect class that only reproduces intermittently in production after a cache fill and is invisible to tests that always run one path first.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `getForLogin` implementation, the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` path and the `idp == null` fallback both explicitly map results through `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(...)`, but the normal cache-hit path returns the raw result of `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` without that mapping. This is a real, diff-grounded inconsistency in wrapping between return paths; whether it becomes a user-visible bug depends on `getById`’s wrapping behavior, which is not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The PR's stated objective is 'add caching support for getForLogin', but the diff silently redefines the getForLogin contract by changing the shared LoginFilter predicate in server-spi so that organization-linked IDPs without BROKER_PUBLIC are excluded, which alters results for every implementation and caller of getForLogin — cached and non-cached alike — without that being part of the announced intent. Any caller of getForLogin outside the organization login page (custom authenticators, third-party providers implementing IdentityProviderStorageProvider) now gets a different set of IDPs than before this PR, with no feature flag or documented API-behavior change; an org-linked IDP that previously appeared in login listings disappears from all login flows, not just the newly cached one.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change shared behavior in a non-local way: `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` in `server-spi` is tightened with `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`, which will exclude organization-linked IDPs unless `BROKER_PUBLIC` is true. That affects all `getForLogin(...)` callers/implementations (cached and non-cached), not just the new Infinispan caching layer. However, from the diff alone this looks intentional (tests added in `OrganizationCacheTest` and usage in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` align with the new rule), so it’s more a scope/API-behavior change concern than a clearly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The added `idp.isEnabled()` re-filter (justified by the comment 'idp might have been wrapped') shows the caching layer changed what getForLogin returns — raw/cached models instead of organization-aware wrapped models — and the burden of preserving the previous behavior was pushed into one caller. Only OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean was patched; any other existing or future caller of IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin that relied on receiving pre-filtered, organization-wrapped models (e.g., other login templates or extensions) now receives un-wrapped models that may be disabled or lack organization context, and will silently render wrong login options.

adjudication.rationale: The new cached-path implementation of `getForLogin` builds the ID list from `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)`, so the cache contents should already reflect the same login predicate/filtering as before. When serving from cache it then resolves each ID via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)`, which goes through the normal `IdentityProviderStorageProvider` chain (and may already apply wrapping/organization-aware behavior in `getById`, not shown in this diff). The finding’s claim that the caching layer now returns “raw/cached models instead of organization-aware wrapped models” and pushes responsibility into one caller is not verifiable from the diff alone, and the diff does not show other callers breaking or `getForLogin` returning disabled IDPs due to caching.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cache-miss path in getForLogin wraps results with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, but the cache-hit path (lines 240-248) resolves IDPs via session.identityProviders().getById(id), which returns the plain cached IdentityProviderModel without the organization-aware wrapping. The organization-aware wrapper is what hides an IDP from the login page when its organization is not public or is member-only (the OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean diff's own 're-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped' comment confirms wrapping can flip enabled state). A user hitting the cached path gets the unwrapped model, so an IDP linked to a non-public organization that was cached under a different organizationId/searchKey context can be rendered on the realm's public login page, disclosing the existence of organization-internal identity providers to unauthenticated users.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`, the cache-miss path explicitly wraps delegate results via `.map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, but the cache-hit path rebuilds the result set by calling `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns those models directly without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. The diff itself shows consumers (in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`) relying on `idp.isEnabled()` potentially being affected by wrapping (comment: "idp might have been wrapped"), so returning unwrapped models on cache-hit can change login-page visibility decisions vs cache-miss. This is an inconsistent behavior introduced by the diff and can expose/enable IDPs that the wrapper would hide for login.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new predicate in getLoginPredicate dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null check, and the whole login-visibility decision for organization-linked IDPs now depends on a string config flag parsed with Boolean.parseBoolean, which silently treats any malformed value (e.g. 'true ', 'yes', 'True ' with whitespace) as non-public. An administrator who sets BROKER_PUBLIC via config map/CLI with any casing/whitespace other than exact 'true' gets an IDP silently hidden from all login pages — an availability/visibility failure with no warning at write time; and if getConfig() returns null (as it can for programmatically built models that never had setConfig called), the predicate throws NPE and breaks the login page entirely.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` adds `idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. This indeed makes login eligibility for org-linked IDPs depend on parsing a String config value without trimming/validation, so values like `"true "` will evaluate to `false` and the IDP will be excluded with no explicit warning. However, the stronger claim that `idp.getConfig()` can be null and will NPE is not verifiable from this diff alone (it depends on `IdentityProviderModel`’s contract/initialization elsewhere).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Login-cache invalidation is triggered only from the IDP create/update/remove paths in this provider; mutations that change which IDPs are login-visible but are performed through the OrganizationProvider (linking/unlinking an IDP to an organization, or disabling the organization itself) do not pass through these methods, so registerIDPLoginInvalidation is never invoked for them. An admin who unlinks an IDP from an organization (or disables the organization) through the organization management endpoints serves stale cached login lists that still expose the old IDP-to-organization mapping on the public login page until some unrelated IDP write invalidates the cache — a stale-authorization-surface window the diff's own test only avoids because it manually calls the IDP update first.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows login-cache invalidation being registered in the IDP storage provider on create/update/remove (registerIDPLoginInvalidation / registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate), but it does not show how OrganizationProvider link/unlink operations are implemented or whether they trigger any cache invalidation elsewhere. Therefore the claim that organization mutations "do not pass through these methods" and will necessarily leave stale login caches cannot be verified from this diff alone. Additionally, the finding’s assertion that the added test "only avoids" staleness because it calls an IDP update first is not supported by the diff: the step-4 update (setting BROKER_PUBLIC) would not trigger invalidation under registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate when organizationId is unchanged and the login predicate remains true for realm-level IDPs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup registration uses the literal alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so every created IDP is leaked into the realm. getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) resolves to a null resource whose remove() is a no-op against a nonexistent alias, so the 20 created IDPs are never cleaned up and pollute subsequent tests in the same realm; the "disabled IDP" test data (e.g. hideOnLogin idp-alias-20 with Broker-20 display name) can break later login-page or IDP-count assertions.
matched_golden_ids: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that cleanup uses the literal alias "alias" instead of constructing "idp-alias-" + i, causing created IDPs not to be removed. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment (incorrect alias in cleanup reference).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new predicate conjunct dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null guard, throwing NPE for IdentityProviderModel instances whose config map is null. Any caller of getLoginPredicate() (including the new InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.registerIDPLoginInvalidation paths on create/update/remove) that passes a model with null config crashes with NullPointerException instead of evaluating the filter; the test suite only feeds admin-API-created IDPs (which always have a config map), so this is untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new conjunct to `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` that calls `idp.getConfig().get(...)` without checking whether `getConfig()` can be null. From the diff alone, it’s clear the predicate would throw an NPE if any `IdentityProviderModel` instance has a null config map, and this predicate is now used in new cache-invalidation paths (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation*`). However, the diff does not establish whether `IdentityProviderModel.getConfig()` is ever null in practice (it may be contractually non-null), so the claimed crash is a plausible edge-case concern but not verifiably a definite defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The test asserts only the cache-entry sizes via IdentityProviderListQuery.getIDPs() and never asserts the contents of the Stream returned by getForLogin(), so the consumer-visible behavior is unverified. A regression in the materialization loop (e.g. the createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapping, ordering, or dropping/duplicating IDPs while the cached id-set stays correct) passes this test; the test would have caught neither a wrong wrapping nor a stream that returns models with wrong organizationId. The assertion `assertEquals(5, identityProviderListQuery.getIDPs("").size())` verifies the cache, not the API contract.

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `testCacheIDPForLogin`, calls to `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` are used only to populate the cache, and assertions are made solely against the internal cache object `IdentityProviderListQuery` via `getIDPs(...).size()` (e.g. `assertEquals(5, identityProviderListQuery.getIDPs("").size())`). The test never terminally inspects the returned `Stream<IdentityProviderModel>` (e.g., collect and assert aliases/org linkage/enabled/public filtering), so a regression in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin()`'s materialization/wrapping path (e.g. `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`, missing/duplicate IDPs, wrong org-aware properties) could slip through while the cached ID set sizes remain correct. This is a concrete coverage gap tied to the added nontrivial caching/materialization logic, not a confirmed functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'cache entry exists but this searchKey is not cached' merge branch (cached == null, invalidateObject + re-add with previous query) is never exercised by the test, which only queries each FetchMode with a single organizationId. The merge constructor new IdentityProviderListQuery(loaded, cacheKey, getRealm(), searchKey, cached, query) and the cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)/addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) sequence run in production whenever two organizations are queried under the same FetchMode in the same realm — the most common multi-org deployment — but the test never calls getForLogin twice with different organizationIds for the same mode, so a broken merge (lost previous searchKeys, wrong revision) ships unverified.

adjudication.rationale: In `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`, the branch where a cached `IdentityProviderListQuery` exists but does not contain the current `searchKey` (`cached = query.getIDPs(searchKey); if (cached == null) { cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey); ... query = new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query); cache.addRevisioned(...) }`) is only executed when the same `FetchMode`/realm is queried with multiple different `organizationId` values (different `searchKey`s). The added test `testCacheIDPForLogin` only ever calls `getForLogin` with a single `organizationId` (`orgaId`) per `FetchMode` (and `null` for REALM_ONLY), so it never exercises the merge constructor path or the invalidateObject+re-add sequence. This is a concrete coverage gap for newly added nontrivial caching logic, not a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The stale-IDP fallback branch inside getForLogin (getById returns null → registerInvalidation and delegate) is untested. The test never simulates a cache entry referencing an IDP that no longer exists (deleted through a non-cached path or cross-node); if this branch throws, mis-sizes, or fails to actually invalidate the cache key, no test in the diff fails. A regression here surfaces as a permanent NPE/empty login page for every user of the affected realm until cache expiry.

adjudication.rationale: The new `getForLogin` caching logic in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin` includes a stale-entry fallback: when iterating cached internal IDs, it does `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and if that returns `null` it calls `realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKey)` and falls back to `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)`. The added test `testCacheIDPForLogin` exercises cache population and invalidation on create/remove/update driven by this same provider, but it never creates a cache entry that references an IDP that later disappears without the login-cache key being invalidated (e.g., cross-node deletion or non-cached path). Therefore the `idp == null` branch (and whether it truly invalidates the login cache key and returns correct results) is indeed untested by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removing an IDP that IS available for login (the registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) call in remove()) is never tested — the test only removes the disabled idp-alias-1 to verify the cache is retained. The invalid direction of remove() is asserted only negatively: if registerIDPLoginInvalidation were dropped or its predicate inverted, every assertion about remove() in testCacheIDPForLogin still passes (removing a non-login IDP expects the cache to remain), so stale removed IDPs would be served on the login page with no failing test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new invalidation logic on removal: `remove()` now calls `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`, which only invalidates login caches when `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)` is true. In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, the only IDP removed is `idp-alias-1`, which is created as disabled (`(i % 2) == 0` means alias-1 is disabled) and thus does not qualify for login; the test asserts caches remain present after that removal. There is no test case removing an IDP that *does* qualify for login (enabled, not hidden, etc.), so a regression where the invalidation call is removed or the predicate logic is wrong would not be caught by this test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new isEnabled() re-filter in searchForIdentityProviders has no test coverage in this diff — the only test file changed (OrganizationCacheTest) exercises storage-level caching, not the login-page bean. The stated reason for the change (wrapped IDPs may have isEnabled cleared by createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel) is never verified: no test asserts that a broker-public organization IDP whose wrapper disables it is excluded from the login-page bean output. A future refactor of the wrapper making the re-check unnecessary, or breaking it, is invisible to the suite.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new logic in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders` to re-filter results with `idp.isEnabled()` (twice), justified by the comment “idp might have been wrapped.” However, the only test changes are in `OrganizationCacheTest`, which exclusively exercises `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin(...)` caching and invalidation (`cacheKeyForLogin`, etc.) and never calls or asserts behavior of the login-page bean. No test in this diff verifies that the bean output excludes a wrapped/organization-aware IDP whose `isEnabled()` may differ after wrapping, so the new behavior and its rationale are unverified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The miss-for-searchKey branch adds the new revisioned query with cache.getCurrentCounter() while the cold-cache branch uses startupRevision, so the newly cached list for a second organizationId is anchored at a later revision than the entry it replaces and its validity is judged against the wrong baseline. A cluster where another node invalidates the login cache between the getCurrentRevision read and the getCurrentCounter write can serve the freshly-cached (already stale) org-specific IDP list indefinitely, so users see a removed/disabled broker on the org login page after the remove()/update() invalidation has already been processed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show an inconsistency in the new `getForLogin` caching logic: the cold-cache path (`query == null`) writes with `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`, while the “searchKey not cached yet” path (`cached == null`) invalidates and then writes with `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. That mismatch is real and could affect how the cache entry’s revision is tracked/validated across invalidations. However, the finding’s specific claim about serving stale data “indefinitely” in a clustered race cannot be verified from this diff alone because the semantics of `addRevisioned`, `startupRevision`, and `getCurrentCounter()` are not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The login-cache invalidation on update() relies on every code path that changes an IDP's organization link going through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update(), but organization membership can also be mutated through the organization provider's IDP management (addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider on the org side), and any such path that writes the link without an update() call bypasses registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate entirely. When an organization links/unlinks a broker via the org API, the cached getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL) sets keep the pre-link IDP lists: a broker just linked to (and hidden from login in) an org continues to be offered on the org's login page, and a broker just unlinked disappears from login until some other invalidation clears the cache — a stale-data condition with no timeout bounded by this code.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new getForLogin() cache keyed by realm+FetchMode and only registers invalidation for that cache from this provider’s create(), update() (via registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate), and remove() methods. The diff itself does not show any invalidation hook tied to organization-side link/unlink operations (e.g., OrganizationProvider identityProviders().addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider), so if those operations can mutate an IDP’s organization association without routing through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update(), this new cache could become stale. However, the diff does not include the org-link implementation, so the bypass is not directly verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The change to the shared getLoginPredicate() silently reclassifies every existing org-linked broker lacking BROKER_PUBLIC=true (config null, so Boolean.parseBoolean(null) is false) as unavailable-for-login across all implementations, not just the new cache. Any existing deployment with organization-linked identity providers that relied on those IDPs appearing via getForLogin(ALL/ORG_ONLY) loses them from the login page at upgrade time with no migration/backfill step setting BROKER_PUBLIC on existing IDP config rows; admins must manually set the flag per broker to restore previous behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the shared `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to additionally require `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. For org-linked IDPs where `BROKER_PUBLIC` is absent/null, `Boolean.parseBoolean(null)` is `false`, so those IDPs will no longer satisfy the login predicate and thus will be filtered out of `getForLogin(...)` results system-wide (not just the new Infinispan caching path). The finding’s point about a silent behavioral/backwards-compatibility change (no migration/backfill shown in this diff) is therefore diff-grounded, though whether it is “wrong” vs. intentional can’t be proven from the diff alone.
